newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices ease with warm weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices ease with warm weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices eased in Wednesday trade as western Canada was blanketed with warm temperatures which were expected to last through the weekend, marketers said.

Spot gas at the AECO hub was quoted at C$1.375/1.38 per gigajoule, down about seven cents from Tuesday and the same level from a week ago. April prices were discussed at about C$1.39 per GJ, also down about seven cents.
Producers and other sellers held off moving volumes on the NOVA Alberta pipeline system for Wednesday, hoping to buy in the spot market for Thursday, a Calgary-based trader said.

"Every producer drafted their NOVA account. Come tommorow we will see the real effects of the warm weather," he said. Those effects were expected to mean another five- to 10-cent drop in AECO prices, he said.
Southern Alberta temperatures were well above freezing after warm Chinook winds blew in on Tuesday.
At the borders, gas at Sumas, Wash. was quoted at between US$1.15 and US$1.20 per million British thermal units, down about 12 cents on the day.

Traders said Westcoast Energy Inc's Pine River gas plant in northern British Columbia was expected to be back at full capacity for Thursday's gas day after a partial outage on Tuesday. The return of processing capacity was seen as a factor behind the price drop.
In the east, Niagara gas was quoted at US$2.27 per mmBtu, down from about US$2.32 on Tuesday.
